cards.text: Jesus has just been arrested. They lead Him away to the high priest, and all the chief priests, elders and scribes gather. Peter, one of Jesus' twelve disciples, follows Him at a distance.

cards.question: Peter is trailing Jesus at a distance. How far does Peter follow Him?

answers.text: Right into the high priest's courtyard
To the city gate and no farther
Back to the garden of Gethsemane

cards.question: Inside the high priest's courtyard, Peter sits with the ___ and warms himself by the ___.

cards.text: Meanwhile, the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin are looking for testimony against Jesus. They want it so they can put Him to death.

cards.question: The Sanhedrin finds plenty of solid testimony against Jesus.

cards.text: Oh, people come forward. MANY people. And they bear false witness against Jesus.

cards.question: The many false witnesses against Jesus all tell the same story.

cards.text: This courtroom is like coworkers retelling one meeting and somehow describing two COMPLETELY different meetings. Then some men stand up and testify falsely against Jesus, with a claim about the temple.

cards.question: These men say they heard Jesus talk about what He'd do with the temple. What do they claim He said?

answers.text: Destroy it and build another in three days
Tear it down and never build again
Rebuild it larger over seven years

cards.text: And even THEIR testimony doesn't line up. So the high priest stands up and questions Jesus: “Have You no answer? What are these men testifying against You?”

cards.question: The high priest presses Jesus to answer the witnesses. What does Jesus do?

cards.text: So the high priest asks Him again, point blank: “Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”

cards.question: When the high priest asks if He is the Christ, Jesus tells him He is.

cards.text: “I am,” Jesus says. Then He adds, “and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”

cards.question: The high priest hears Jesus' answer. What does he do with his clothes?
The high priest says they don't need any more witnesses. He tells the council they've heard the ___.
The high priest asks for a verdict, and the council all condemn Jesus as deserving of ___.

cards.text: Then some of them start to spit on Jesus. They blindfold Him, hit Him with their fists, and say to Him, “Prophesy!”

cards.question: Jesus is blindfolded and beaten. How do the officers receive Him?

cards.text: Meanwhile, Peter is still down in the courtyard. One of the high priest's servant girls comes down and sees him warming himself by the fire.

cards.question: The servant girl takes a good look at Peter by the fire. What does she say to him?

answers.text: You were with Jesus the Nazarene
You must be one of the officers
You need to leave this courtyard

cards.question: The servant girl says Peter was with Jesus. How does Peter answer her?

answers.text: He says he doesn't know what she means
He says yes and he's proud of it
He tells her to go ask the officers

cards.text: Friend, that's a full-on “new phone, who dis.” Then Peter heads out to the gateway.

cards.question: Peter heads out to the gateway of the high priest's courtyard. What happens right then?

cards.text: Peter moves to the gateway, and the servant girl spots him THERE too. It's like dodging someone at the store, switching aisles, and BOOM, there they are again.

cards.question: This time, the servant girl tells the people standing nearby that Peter is one of Jesus' followers.
Peter gets called out a second time by the servant girl, and he ___ it again.

cards.text: After a little while, the people standing nearby try one more time. And now they've got a reason.

cards.question: The people nearby tell Peter he's surely one of Jesus' followers, because he's a ___ too.
Called out a third time, Peter finally admits he knows Jesus.

cards.text: Instead, Peter begins to curse and swear: “I do not know this man of whom you speak!” And immediately, the rooster crows a second time.

cards.question: Right then, Peter remembers what Jesus told him: before the rooster crows ___ times, Peter will deny Him ___ times.

cards.text: Those words come rushing back to Peter: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.”

cards.question: Peter remembers what Jesus said about the rooster. What does Peter do?

answers.text: He goes back to the fire

cards.text: And that's where we leave Peter for now. Hold on, friend, because this story is FAR from finished.

findings.problem: The opening card states two facts from outside the passage: 'Jesus has just been arrested' (Mark 14:46) and 'Peter, one of Jesus' twelve disciples' (Mark 3:14-16). Neither carries its reference. The card's verses field cites only Mark 14:53-54.
findings.question: Prep allows facts from outside the passage 'with their reference', and 'Cite exactly what the card uses.' The card JSON has only one verses field, and the script checks references against the passage. Where should an outside fact's reference go on a story card? Should it go in the verses field (e.g. 'Mark 14:46, 53-54'), in the card text, or should outside facts like these go uncited as context?

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'servants' for the first blank is close to 'officers'. The officers in the high priest's courtyard are his servants, and the passage itself has the high priest's servant girls in that courtyard (Mark 14:66). A baker could argue that Peter sat with the servants.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Card 4 already tells the baker that the Sanhedrin wants testimony 'so they can put Him to death.' That gives away card 17's blank, 'deserving of ___' (death), and rules out prison and exile. Card 17 needs a different question, or different wording.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'blasphemy' is the only answer that sounds like the Bible or a courtroom. 'gossip' and 'riddle' are a different tone and kind of thing, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Several story cards in stop 1 are plain retelling with no Papa Dorin voice. Card 12 adds only 'point blank.' Card 14 is just the quote. Card 18 is a straight list of the abuse. Outside card 8, the stop reads like a summary, not a storyteller. The added voice can be reverent, such as a quiet storyteller's line, and needn't be a joke, but these cards need some of him.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The comparison 'dodging someone at the store, switching aisles' says Peter went to the gateway to avoid the servant girl. Mark 14:68-69 never says why Peter went out to the gateway. The card also says again that Peter moves to the gateway, which card 4 already told.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: In 'and he ___ it again,' the word 'again' rules out 'admits', because Peter never admitted anything before. Only 'denies' and 'ignores' are left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats the words of Jesus that card 13 just asked about. It doesn't move the passage forward.
